name: Section Entropy Imbalances Form the Incidence Cycle Space
statement: Let $G_D$ be the bipartite incidence graph between the minimal missing patterns of the common section $D$ and its coordinates, with one edge for every section coefficient entry. Every feasible local entropy imbalance $\omega$ lies in the real cycle space $Z_D$: its entries sum to zero at every pattern vertex and every coordinate vertex. Moreover $\|\omega\|_1\leq2m$ for local mass $m$, and $\dim Z_D=|E(G_D)|-|V(G_D)|+\operatorname{comp}(G_D)$.
proof: Within each comparison, unfavorable and selected favorable masses agree, so summing coefficient contributions over one row gives zero. Summing the internal witness-balance equations over all concepts leaves zero total imbalance at each shared coordinate. The favorable and unfavorable section contributions each have total mass at most $m$, yielding the norm bound. Changing signs on one bipartition identifies these conservation equations with the oriented incidence equations of $G_D$.
comments: A spanning forest supplies the usual fundamental-cycle basis. The theorem adds that both concept-class incidence relations force the entropy interface into this cycle space.
